coverage_note: Whole file read in order. Left out as S4 pronunciation: وجهّزت shadda 03:13, صلاحتو→صلحته 08:11 (vowel length), قربان for خربان 07:46, أزعشتك 15:02, سكرتي/سهوني/يسكر letter-order slips 29:46/33:41/34:14 ('The K is before the S'), إن كسر→انكسر spacing 49:31, إيدها انكسرت letter order 43:10, ولا اشي→إشي vowel 52:52, بعيم for بقيم 27:05, بفزت for ببسّط 56:04, تباين for تبعي 48:31. Three letter-order slips that produced real other words (زعمت, بخسر, تعبي) ARE written as low-confidence vocab rows because Amal treated them as words and Medi asked (04:05) that such fixes be marked. Latin-transliterated stretch 06:38-07:20 (date and clock). Garbled/unreadable Medi lines not judged: 19:36-19:39 (مين أزعجك), 19:54 أشيك تير, 24:50 بتدايك, 30:02-30:21 (we broke your windows), 38:33 Amal 'أشياءي نوع الإل' (unclear, he says he did not say el-), 42:05-42:15 (hand), 54:24 إمّني, 55:05 أبن كتير, 55:30 بفيت, 55:33 Amal 'أنا واعي'. English-only stretches: 03:40-05:51 (recording rules), 17:06-18:06, 46:08-48:13, 57:37-1:01:49 (causative verbs). Drill slips during conjugation runs (45:24 بينكسري, 45:34) and self-fixes (13:37, 29:46, 34:20, 05:58) not written. Amal used English 'air conditioning' herself (48:29) and مكيف is not on her sheet, so his 'air conditioning' is not tier 3; YouTube, bones not on sheet.

rows.medi_said: كيف كان الـ-- كيف كان العروسة؟ عروس؟
rows.why: عروس is the bride, عرس is the wedding; she recast عرس and he still repeated عروس at 01:57.

زعم (claimed) for عزم (invited; sheet: i invited | Ana 3azamet | أنا عزمت); a letter-order slip that may be S4 pronunciation, but she recast it twice (03:02, 04:11) and Medi flagged it himself at 04:05 as a word that should be marked wrong.

rows.medi_said: tisa / asha. Oh no, that's right. Yeah, asha tisa.
rows.why: Date said month-first (tisa asha = 9 10) before switching to day-first; she stated the day-then-month order. He half self-fixed before her line, so low.

rows.medi_said: Sa alaat ila nun-- ila tult.
rows.why: Clock hour: he said talaat (three) where the time was two (tintayn); she asked three or two, he fixed to Intayn and she confirmed تنتين إلا تلت at 07:22. Could also be a plain number slip.
The weather as a known thing takes el- (sheet: it's hot | El-jaw shoab | الجو شوب); the adjective شوب is missing or lost by the transcript. She replied عن جد and let it pass.
رن takes على (sheet: i call | Ana barenn (3ala) | أنا برن); he used لـ. Amal let it pass.

rows.medi_said: Is it raki? What was electricity?
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked for 'electricity' and she supplied كهربا (sheet: electricity | Kahraba | كهربا).

rows.medi_said: مهندس-- Do you guys say مهندس كهرباء؟
rows.why: Idafa: the owner noun takes el-, the first never; he asked with no el- and she recast مهندس الكهربا; he repeated it right at 09:07.

rows.amal_said: Or some people say كهربجي. It's easier.
rows.why: Didn't-know: she volunteered the everyday word كهربجي; he had never attempted it. Not on her sheet (Medi says so at 09:39).

rows.medi_said: كراجي. This is a new word. It's not gonna be on the list.
rows.why: كراجي (garage hand) is a different word from كهربجي; he said it at 09:30 and 09:39 and she recast.

rows.medi_said: ما، ما يكون، uh, كهربج-- uh, كهربجي، هو مهندس، uh, مهندس.
rows.why: Describing the man he called yesterday (past): needs ما كان; ykoon belongs after lamma/iza or for habits (B8). She did not react.
rows.english: He wasn't an electrician, he was an engineer

rows.amal_said: You said صلح which is fix. You did wha-- did you wanna say he helped me?
rows.why: صلح = fix used for 'help'; she asked what he meant and he produced ساعدني at 11:07 (sheet: help | Saa3ed | ساعد).
'For me' rides on the preposition (لي), not as an object ending on the verb (صلحني = he fixed me, 10:44); she separated the two forms.
rows.english: He fixed (it) for me a bit

rows.why: بلوزة is feminine so the colour adjective is feminine; her line is garbled (likely وردية) but he answered 'وردنية that's right' and she said صح at 12:16. Her sheet has pink | Zahri | زهري.
Non-form with an extra ن for pink; her صح at 12:16 seems to answer لأول مرة. Sheet: pink (m/f) | Zahri | زهري.
Wrong shape of 'I stayed' (sheet: i stayed/kept | Ana dallait | أنا ضليت); ض/د could be S4 but the vowel shape is off too and she did not understand ('what?') before recasting.
'Stayed (at) my house' needs a preposition; he had none, she asked بِ أو فِي and he fixed to بي بيتي at 12:50.
'One X' is noun then وحدة; he put the number first and she recast.

rows.medi_said: بس كلمة-- بس فعل، اه، تنين،
rows.why: Two of a noun takes the dual فعلين, not the bare number; her reply is garbled (may itself be فعلين) so filed as let-pass.
rows.english: just one word, well, two verbs

rows.amal_said: بتحب نشوف الواجب أو الفعل اللي بعده؟
rows.why: He asks her to repeat; كم مرة = how many times. Sheet: one more time | Kaman marra | كمان مرة. She just rephrased her question.
English calque 'one more' with أكتر; she gave كمان واحد and he repeated it.
Feminine subject needs the feminine participle; she asked إنتي أو انت and he fixed to مزعوجة at 18:54.

rows.medi_said: And then باز is not بازوج, بازيجيني هدول اليوم.
rows.why: Plural subject (many things) needs the plural verb ending -u; she recast بزعجوني and offered بتزعجني as the other option at 20:18.
rows.english: Many things annoy me these days

rows.why: Same agreement miss repeated on the second attempt; she recast again and he fixed to بيزعجوني at 20:33.
'These days' needs the plural أيام; he used the singular and she recast.

rows.medi_said: أيام. I even wrote أيام. هدول أيام.
rows.why: The noun after هدول keeps its el-; he dropped it in the fixed version and she moved on (طيب).
'Sure THAT you didn't' is إنو, not the relative اللي; she asked 'Why اللي؟' at 21:27 and stated إنو مش اللي.
rows.english: Are you sure that you (pl) didn't annoy him?

rows.why: 'Annoy HIM' needs the object ending -o on the verb; she was busy with اللي and let it pass.

rows.amal_said: بس مبسوطة إذا ما بشوف هيك.
rows.why: After إذا ما her recast keeps the b- (إذا ما بشوفك مبسوطة); he had the bare form and repeated hers at 22:31. Filed under the iza-verb rule although the bucket text says drop; her form is the reference.
rows.english: I get annoyed if I don't see you happy

rows.why: He gave a positive command for 'don't be annoyed'; she prompted and he produced ما تنزعج then ما تنزعجي (23:24-23:32).
'With them' is the ending on the preposition (منهم), not a separate pronoun; she had said بعدين and let it pass.
'Their intention' is the ending on the noun (قصدهم, sheet: intention | Qaṣd | قصد); the transcript shows a separate pronoun, which may be spacing. She moved on to the next part.

After مش قصدهم ('it wasn't their intention to') the verb is bare, no b-; she recast يدايقوكي and he kept the b- ('أنا بعرف هيك', 25:16). ق→ت is pronunciation, not counted. Sheet: i upset someone | Ana badaaye2 | أنا بدايق.
rows.english: They didn't mean to upset you

rows.why: Second use of كم مرة (how many times) to ask her to repeat; sheet: one more time | Kaman marra | كمان مرة. She just repeated herself.
He groped for 'to remove' and she supplied بقيم (sheet: i remove / take away | Ana ba2eem | أنا بقيم); his fragment may have been بشيل, which is also usable. His later بعيم is a dropped ق (S4).

rows.medi_said: الـ أول الـ فعل، الـ أول الكلمة.
rows.why: Idafa: the first word never takes el-; he put el- on both. She answered Mm and let it pass.
rows.english: the beginning of the verb / of the word

rows.why: بخسر means 'I lose', a different word; likely a خ/ك hard-letter slip (S4/F1). She said قريب and recast; he repeated بخسر at 28:06, 28:18 and 28:26.
'They broke' needs the -u ending; her questioning echo made him fix to هم كسروا at 28:47, which she confirmed.
Plain present needs the b-; he gave the bare form for هم and she said Nice at the next form.
-تم is the MSA you-plural past; Levantine is -توا (his own كسرتوا at 29:18). She said طيب and moved on.
'His cups' needs the plural كاسات before the ending; he used the singular with -o and she recast.
For 'his cup' she gave كاسه (sheet: cup | Kaasa | كاسة); his form keeps a -t- before the ending. Levantine also says كاستو, so low.
كاسة is feminine so the verb takes -t; she recast and he saw it ('because it's female', 40:57).
عمر is masculine so كان, not كانت, even though 'she' is the person; he pushed كانت twice (43:36, 43:43) and she said لأ.
rows.english: when she was twelve (when her age was 12)

rows.why: Eleven for twelve (sheet: eleven | e7da3sh | إحداعش; twelve | tna3sh | تنعش); she said 12 then إتناش and he used اثنعش at 44:18.
He put a feminine ending on the noun مضارع (present tense) and repeated المضارعة at 44:41 after her recast.

rows.medi_said: إن كسر / من-- من الحرارة or
rows.amal_said: انكسر. Did it actually like break?
rows.why: انكسر is physical breaking; for the AC stopping he needs خرب/خربان (sheet: not working properly | 5arbaan | خربان; i break down | Ana ba5rab | بخرب). She said 'my issue is with the verb itself... It's physical' at 49:51.
rows.english: The air conditioning broke (stopped working) from the heat

rows.why: 'I have never broken anything' is past; he thought أبدًا forces the present and she corrected (52:10-52:23: أبداً ما + past), he fixed to ما كسرت at 52:36.
He meant تبعي (mine, as she gave at 48:29); the letter-order slip made 'tired me' and she heard it that way (53:25). May be S4 metathesis; he dropped the word on retry (53:29).
Negation goes on the verb with ما, not مش before the adverb; she recast and he repeated ما نمت منيح at 53:54.

rows.amal_said: شو هم الـ unverbs، الـ أن verbs اللي أخذناهم؟
rows.why: English inside an Arabic question while the word is on her sheet (verb – verbs | Fe3el | فعل); but she herself said 'الـ unverbs' first and he was echoing her term in a meta question, so likely not an error.
rows.english: What verbs did we do today?

rows.medi_said: إن و-- إن. الف-الفعلات. الفعلات إن.
rows.why: Invented -at plural for the broken plural أفعال; she recast and he said الأفعال at 54:53. The brief also lists an invented plural as vocab tier 2; arbiter's call.
Active participle (annoying) for the passive (annoyed); sheet: annoyed | Maz3ooj | مزعوج vs annoying | Muz3ej | مزعج. She recast and he fixed at 56:47.

rows.medi_said: is it بزور بنكسر؟ بنكسر. أكسر. Okay.
rows.why: Naming the verb pair he gave أكسر without the b-; she restated بكسر and بنكسر.
Replying to her يلا بشوفك ('see you') he negated a past verb ('I didn't see you'); may be a transcription of منشوفك. She just said باي.
